corpus: original model suggestions with verified insertion in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base, pooled and donor advantage is excluded under both interval methods; uniform advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling. All primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor and pooled useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods; all residual intervals include zero, including the narrowly positive pooled writer upper endpoint. Residual uniform useful advantage is excluded under both methods. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods. Raw pooled comparison favors personal adaptation at zero under both methods, but neither interval clears the useful margin; raw base and donor intervals include zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Selected model text reflects both suggestion supply and prior human selection, not human prose authorship or a uniquely identified preference mechanism. Sparse histories, fixed donor/global training, shared exposed human units and differing corpus support preclude seed/backbone/corpus rankings, independent human confirmation, population limits, private-goal inference or a whole-matrix verdict. Historical failures and unknown attempts stay separate; no new retry.
